rounds.text: Krystal Integrated Services Ltd trades at a compelling P/E of just 11.4x and a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.50x, offering an attractive entry point relative to its fundamental delivery [E1, E2]. The company exhibits robust historical compounding, generating a 5-year compounded sales growth of 22% and a standout 5-year profit growth CAGR of 30% [E14, E53]. Profitability metrics decisively outpace sector benchmarks, with a reported ROCE of 16.2% and ROE of 13.8%, comfortably beating the sector median ROCE of 7.0% [E10, E12, E13, E67]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis estimates intrinsic value at ₹ 2069 per share against the current market price of ₹ 580, leaving a massive margin of safety of 72.0% where the current market price implies a negligible earnings growth of just 0.5% [E39, E40, E41]. Conceded: institutional shareholding has declined with foreign and domestic institutions reducing stakes, borrowings have increased to ₹ 153 Cr in Sep 2026, and working capital days have risen to 77.6 days [E33, E36, E37, E55]. Despite these near-term capital headwinds, recent operational performance is accelerating with net profit up 46% year-on-year, showing that fundamental results are significantly outpacing cautious market sentiment [E59, E63].

Krystal Integrated Services faces significant headwinds regarding its capital efficiency and institutional support. While the company reports profit growth, the cash conversion ratio of 0.41x for March 2026 indicates that reported profits are significantly outpacing actual cash generation, raising concerns about the quality of earnings [E28]. This is compounded by a deterioration in working capital efficiency, as days have increased from 52.5 to 77.6 [E55]. Furthermore, the company is experiencing a notable exodus of professional capital, with foreign institutional holdings dropping from 7.95% to 1.46% and domestic institutions reducing their stake by 2.05 percentage points since March 2024 [E36, E37]. The stock’s technical position remains weak, trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, which aligns with the negative institutional money flow [E38, E44]. Borrowings have also escalated to Rs 153 Cr from Rs 120 Cr in the prior year, adding pressure to the balance sheet [E33]. Conceded: the company maintains a solid 5-year compounded profit growth of 30% and a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x [E17, E31].

Conceded: the cash conversion is 0.41x for March 2026 and working capital days have increased from 52.5 to 77.6 [E28, E55]. However, the business still generated Rs 26 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 11 Cr in free cash flow, proving it is actively turning earnings into tangible cash [E29, E30]. Conceded: borrowings rose to Rs 153 Cr from Rs 120 Cr, and institutional holdings saw a decline [E33, E36, E37]. Despite this temporary technical weakness below moving averages, the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28x alongside a comfortable current ratio of 2.01x [E31, E32, E44]. Furthermore, looking past stale sentiment, actual business results are rapidly accelerating with a 46% year-on-year surge in net profit that vastly outpaces one-year price growth [E51, E59, E63].

Conceded: the company generated Rs 26 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 11 Cr in free cash flow [E29, E30]. However, this is undermined by a poor cash conversion ratio of just 0.41x, indicating that reported profits are heavily outstripping actual cash generation due to receivables or accruals [E28]. Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio sits at a conservative 0.28x alongside a 2.01x current ratio [E31, E32]. Despite these liquidity comforts, total borrowings expanded significantly to Rs 153 Cr from Rs 120 Cr a year earlier [E33]. Conceded: net profit surged 46% year-on-year [E59]. Yet this profit acceleration is clouded by working capital days worsening sharply from 52.5 to 77.6 days [E55] and an inconsistent yearly operating margin trend [E26]. Finally, dismissing institutional outflows and price weakness as stale sentiment ignores the sustained negative money flow and technical damage where the stock remains below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E38, E44, E61, E63].
